executiveSummary: Checkout p99 latency doubled as traffic grew because every cart line item made its own call to pricing. Batching the calls and caching hot prices in-process for 30 seconds cut p99 by 60%, from 1.84 s to 0.74 s at peak, cut database CPU by 38%, and lifted conversion 2.1%. The talk shows the trace, the one-loop change, the rollout, and the decision to accept 30 seconds of staleness.

slides.subtitle: Payments platform · Engineering all-hands, Q3 2026

slides.slideTitle: At last year's peak, one checkout in a hundred took almost two seconds
keyBullets: p99 checkout latency at the Black Friday peak, 2025
slides.speakerNotes:
- 1.84 seconds at p99.
- At that latency, carts abandon at twice the normal rate.
slides.purpose: States the problem as one number
slides.intent: Make the cost of the slowness felt

slides.slideTitle: Latency climbed every week as traffic grew
slides.subtitle: p99 checkout latency, ms
keyBullets: p99 doubled in eight weeks, from 910 ms to 1,840 ms
slides.speakerNotes: - The trend lines up with traffic, week for week.
slides.purpose: Shows the trend that forced the work
slides.intent: Make them see it was getting worse, not a blip

slides.slideTitle: Every line item made its own call to pricing
slides.subtitle: How a checkout request flows today
keyBullets: Edge: CDN and API gateway
Checkout service: Go, 40 pods
Pricing service: one synchronous call per line item
Postgres: one primary, two read replicas
slides.speakerNotes:
- A cart of twelve items makes twelve calls to pricing.
- Each call is fast. Twelve in a row is not.
slides.intent: Make the bottleneck obvious from the picture

slides.subtitle: checkout/price.go
keyBullets: Before: for _, item := range cart.Items { p, err := pricing.Get(ctx, item.SKU) }
After: prices, err := pricing.GetMany(ctx, cart.SKUs())
slides.speakerNotes:
- Before: N calls. After: one.
- The pricing service already had a batch endpoint. Nobody used it.
slides.intent: Make engineers see how small the change was

slides.slideTitle: Four steps took it from idea to production
keyBullets: Measure: trace every checkout for a week
Batch: one pricing call per cart
Cache: keep hot prices in-process for 30 s
Roll out: 1%, 10%, 50%, 100% over nine days
slides.speakerNotes:
- Each step shipped on its own.
- The rollout took nine days because we watched error rates at each step.

slides.slideTitle: Pricing went from most of the request to a sliver
slides.subtitle: Time per stage at p99, ms
keyBullets: Pricing fell from 1,210 ms to 140 ms at p99
slides.speakerNotes:
- Database and network barely moved.
- Pricing was the whole story.
slides.purpose: Compares where the time went before and after

slides.slideTitle: Faster checkout, cheaper database, more orders
keyBullets: −60%: p99 checkout latency
0.74 s: p99 at this year's peak
−38%: database CPU
+2.1%: checkout conversion
slides.speakerNotes: - The conversion lift alone pays for the quarter.

slides.slideTitle: We keep the cache in-process, not in Redis
slides.subtitle: Decision brief · Platform council, 14 Oct
keyBullets: Decision: keep hot prices in each pod's memory for 30 seconds
Why: one network hop fewer, and no new cluster to run
Trade-off: a price change can take up to 30 seconds to reach every pod
Ask: approve 30 s as the standard staleness for pricing
slides.speakerNotes:
- Redis would have added a hop and a cluster.
- The cost is staleness, and finance agreed 30 seconds is fine.
slides.purpose: Records the decision and its cost
slides.intent: Make the council approve the trade-off

slides.slideTitle: “The pager stayed quiet all of Black Friday”
keyBullets: The pager stayed quiet all of Black Friday. That has never happened before.
Dana Okafor, payments on-call lead
slides.speakerNotes:
- Dana was on call for peak.
- This is the quote I'm proudest of.
slides.purpose: Puts a human voice on the result
slides.intent: Make the team feel the win

keyBullets: Trace before you tune: the traces found the loop in a day
Use the endpoint you already have: the batch API was two years old
Roll out in steps you can watch: four stages caught two bugs
slides.speakerNotes: - None of these are new. All of them are easy to skip.
slides.intent: Make other teams copy the method
